title: Operational GovOps can block a rebate distribution outright and must publish its reasons when it does
content:
A.6.1.1.8.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3 sets the check on self-assessment: "Operational GovOps reviews Launch Agent 7's calculation of the rebate before executing a return of surplus to token holders. In the event of any issues, Operational GovOps cannot execute the distribution."

The prohibition is phrased as incapacity rather than discretion — "cannot execute" — which removes the option of proceeding under protest with a note in the file. Any unresolved issue stops the money.

The threshold is deliberately low: "any issues," not material misstatement or bad faith. That is a strong asymmetry in favour of not paying, and it is coherent with the surrounding design, since a distribution once made to token holders is effectively unrecoverable while a delayed one is not.

Against that power sit two duties that make it costly to exercise casually. GovOps "must post an explanation on the Sky Forum under the 'Launch Agent 7 Prime' category" — the same public venue used for Root Edit findings — and "must work with Launch Agent 7 to resolve the disagreement." A blocking decision is therefore public, reasoned, and paired with an obligation to fix rather than merely refuse.

The recurring shape across this Artifact is worth noting: operational actors are given veto-shaped powers, and the only structural constraint applied to them is mandatory public reasoning.
description: Review is a hard gate: if there are any issues GovOps cannot execute the distribution, must post an explanation on the Sky Forum, and must work with the Agent toward resolution.
